mainTopic: The age for giving rulings, the seven kinds of fake פרושין, whether merit delays the bitter water, and a סוטה's מנחה that became טמא
overview: This amud starts by finishing a discussion about a student who gives halachic rulings too early. The גמרא says the too-early period lasts until forty years. It then challenges this from רבה, and answers that a younger scholar may rule if he is equal to the leading scholar of his city. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's phrase 'מכות פרושין' with a ברייתא that lists seven kinds of fake or overdone פרושין, and explains each type. אביי and רבא say the last two types (from love and from fear) should be removed from the list, because רב teaches that doing מצוות שלא לשמה leads to לשמה. רב נחמן בר יצחק warns that the Heavenly court will punish those who only look righteous. ינאי המלך tells his wife to beware of hypocrites who act like זמרי but want the reward of פנחס. A new משנה follows: רבי שמעון says merit does not delay the bitter water, while רבי says it does, but the guilty woman slowly wastes away. The amud ends with the law of a סוטה's מנחה that became טמא, and opens a list of women whose מנחות are burned. The list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How long must a student wait before ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a student is considered too early to issue halachic rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And until how long is it too early for him to rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how long a student must wait before he may give rulings. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא discussed a student who gives rulings before he has reached the level of הוראה. Now it wants a clear time limit for how long that 'too early' period lasts.

phrases.english: And until how long?
phrases.notes: He means: until when is a student still too early to give rulings, the topic the גמרא was just discussing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about a student who rules too early.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of time during which a student is considered too early to issue rulings.

steps.title: The answer: forty years
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the too-early period lasts until forty years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a fixed number as the general rule. The next step will test this rule against a real person who did not fit it.

phrases.english: Until forty years.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The too-early period lasts until forty years.

steps.title: But רבה gave rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the forty-year rule from רבה, who gave rulings even though he lived only forty years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבה gave rulings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the forty-year rule by pointing to רבה, who gave rulings anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה lived only forty years in total, so he must have given rulings before reaching the forty-year mark. If the rule were absolute, a great sage like רבה would have been doing something wrong.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But רבה gave rulings!
phrases.notes: רבה lived only forty years, so he ruled before reaching that point.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not rule before forty years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה, an accepted sage, ruled even though he lived only forty years, so the rule cannot be absolute.

steps.title: Allowed when he is equal to the city's leading scholar
steps.stepSummary: Ruling earlier is allowed when the student is equal in knowledge to the leading scholar of his city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ruling before forty is allowed if the scholar is equal to the leading sage of his city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forty-year rule is the normal case. If a younger scholar's knowledge already matches the top scholar in town, he may rule, and that is how רבה could rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A student should not rule before forty years, unless his knowledge equals that of the leading scholar of his city.

phrases.english: When they are equal.
phrases.notes: He means: when the younger scholar is as learned as the greatest scholar in his city.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule with an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forty-year limit applies to everyone, so רבה's rulings are a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit does not apply to someone equal to the leading scholar of his city, like רבה.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: 'blows of the פרושין'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase about the injuries of the פרושין to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the blows of the פרושין,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its words about the 'blows of the פרושין.' This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the 'blows of the פרושין' among things that ruin the world. The גמרא now wants to explain who these פרושין are.

keyTerms.meaning: People who separate themselves to look pious; here, fake or overdone piety
And so on (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: And the blows of the פרושין, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה counts the 'blows of the פרושין' among things that ruin the world.

steps.title: The ברייתא: seven kinds of פרושין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists seven types of פרושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are seven kinds of פרושין: the שכם-type, the foot-bruising type, the head-bleeding type, the pestle type, the 'what is my obligation and I will do it' type, the one from love, and the one from fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that names seven kinds of פרושין. The next steps will explain them one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is a short nickname describing a different way of looking pious falsely or in an overdone way. Only the names are given here; the meanings come in the following lines.
steps.confusionAlert: Being 'פרוש מאהבה' or 'פרוש מיראה' sounds good, but here they are on a list of problem types. Wait for the גמרא's explanation before deciding what they mean.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There are seven kinds of פרושין:
The שכם-type פרוש, the foot-bruising פרוש,
the head-bleeding פרוש, the pestle פרוש,
the פרוש who says, 'What is my obligation, and I will do it,'
the פרוש from love, and the פרוש from fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to explain the משנה's term from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are seven types of פרושין.

steps.title: The שכם type and the foot-bruising type
steps.stepSummary: The first type acts like the people of שכם, and the second bruises his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שכם-type פרוש is one who does the deed of שכם. The foot-bruising פרוש is one who bruises his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first two names on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of שכם agreed to a מצוה (מילה) only for personal gain, so the שכם-type does good deeds only to be honored. The foot-bruising type drags his feet to look humble and ends up hurting them.

keyTerms.meaning: Of שכם, like the people of שכם
The deed of שכם (doing a מצוה for gain)

phrases.english: The שכם-type פרוש:
this is one who does the deed of שכם.
phrases.notes: The people of שכם agreed to מילה only for profit (בראשית 34); so too, he acts pious only for honor.

phrases.english: The foot-bruising פרוש:
this is one who bruises his feet.
phrases.notes: He shuffles slowly to look humble and keeps knocking his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוּשׁ שִׁיכְמִי — זֶה הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה שְׁכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the list from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכם-type acts pious for gain; the foot-bruising type injures his feet showing off humility.

steps.title: The head-bleeding type
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that this type bleeds from banging into walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: The head-bleeding פרוש: רב נחמן בר יצחק said, this is one who lets blood against the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the third name on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person walks with his eyes shut, supposedly so he will not look at women, and so he bangs into walls and bleeds. His show of modesty causes him harm.

phrases.english: The head-bleeding פרוש:
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
this is one who lets blood against the walls.
phrases.notes: He walks with his eyes closed to look modest, so he bumps his head into walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוּשׁ קִיזַּאי — אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the list, now with a named אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The head-bleeding type bangs into walls because of his showy modesty.

steps.title: The pestle type
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא explains that this type walks bent over like a pestle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pestle פרוש: רבה בר שילא said, one who is bent over like a pestle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא explains the fourth name on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person walks hunched over, like the pestle used in a mortar, to look humble. Again the piety is only an outward show.

phrases.english: The pestle פרוש:
Rabba bar Sheila said:
one who is bent over like a pestle.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוּשׁ מְדוּכְיָא — אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pestle type walks hunched over to look humble.

steps.title: Why is 'what is my obligation' a bad thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why someone who wants to know his obligations is on a list of bad types.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פרוש who says 'What is my obligation, and I will do it.' But that is a good quality!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fifth name: wanting to know your obligation and doing it sounds like a good thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other type so far was clearly showing off. This one seems to be a sincere person who wants to fulfill his duties, so why is he counted among those who ruin the world?

phrases.english: The פרוש who says, 'What is my obligation, and I will do it.'
But that is a good quality!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the fifth name on the list and questions why it belongs there.
steps.kashyaTarget: Including 'מה חובתי ואעשנה' among the bad פרושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking about one's obligations in order to fulfill them is praiseworthy, not harmful.

steps.title: He is asking for more obligations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he says 'what MORE is my obligation,' as if he has already done everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means one who says, 'What further obligation do I have, and I will do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this person is really asking what else is left for him to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding one word, תו ('more'), changes everything: he is claiming he has already done every מצוה perfectly. That is arrogance dressed up as piety.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'מה חובתי ואעשנה' type is bad because he means 'what MORE should I do,' boasting that he has already done everything.

phrases.english: Rather, it is one who says:
'What further obligation do I have, and I will do it.'
phrases.notes: He is hinting that he has already done all his מצוות perfectly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר מָה חוֹבָתִי תּוּ וְאֶעֱשֶׂנָּה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the phrase by adding the word תו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He sincerely wants to know his basic obligations, which is praiseworthy.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is asking what MORE he can do, implying he has already fulfilled everything, which is arrogance.

steps.title: The last two types: serving out of love and serving out of fear
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the sixth and seventh types of פרוש: one who serves out of love and one who serves out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another type is a פרוש out of love, and another is a פרוש out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא's list of seven types of פרושים by giving the last two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two keep the מצוות, but for a personal reason. One does it because he loves the reward, and the other because he fears the punishment. The ברייתא counts them as flawed because they are not serving purely for the sake of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: One who keeps מצוות out of love for the reward
One who keeps מצוות out of fear of punishment

phrases.english: One who is 'separated' out of love,
phrases.notes: He means love of the reward he will get, not love of ה׳.

phrases.english: one who is 'separated' out of fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of seven types after the explanation of 'what more is my obligation'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא counts the פרוש who acts out of love or out of fear among the flawed types.

steps.title: אביי and רבא say to remove the last two types
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא tell the תנא not to teach these two types, because רב said that learning and doing מצוות שלא לשמה leads to doing them לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא said to the תנא: Do not teach 'a פרוש out of love, a פרוש out of fear.' This is because רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always be busy with תורה and מצוות even if it is not for their own sake, because doing it not for its own sake leads to doing it for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא object to part of the ברייתא and tell the תנא to remove the last two types from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats serving for reward or out of fear as a bad trait. אביי and רבא answer from רב's teaching that this kind of service is actually a good beginning, because it brings a person to pure service. So these two do not belong on a list of bad types.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who memorized and recited ברייתות in the בית מדרש
Not for its own sake, for a personal motive
For its own sake, purely for Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: Even a מצוה done for the wrong reason is worth doing, because it leads to doing it for the right reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's teaching of מתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה is a basic rule about how a person grows in עבודת השם.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava said to the tanna:
Do not teach
'one separated out of love, one separated out of fear,'
because Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should always busy himself with Torah and מצוות
even if not for their own sake,
because from doing it not for its own sake, he comes to do it for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא לְתַנָּא: לָא תִּיתְּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inclusion of the two types just listed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's inclusion of the פרוש מאהבה and the פרוש מיראה as bad types.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב teaches that serving שלא לשמה is a good path to לשמה, so these people should not be counted as flawed.

steps.title: Heaven will punish those who pretend to be righteous
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that what is hidden stays hidden from people, but the Heavenly court will punish those who wrap themselves in the cloak of the righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is hidden is hidden, and what is revealed is revealed. The great court will collect payment from those who wrap themselves in cloaks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a general warning about people who look pious but are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People can only judge what they see on the outside. A fake צדיק may fool everyone, but the Heavenly court sees what is hidden and will punish him for the pretending.

keyTerms.meaning: Cloaks, the outer garments of the pious

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is hidden is hidden,
and what is revealed is revealed,
phrases.notes: He means that people only judge what they can see, but Heaven sees everything.

phrases.english: the great court will collect payment
from those who wrap themselves in cloaks.
phrases.notes: The cloak stands for looking like a צדיק on the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דְּמִטַּמְּרָא מִטַּמְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a general statement about fake piety after the list of פרושים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Heavenly court will punish those who pretend to be righteous.

steps.title: ינאי המלך warns his wife about hypocrites
steps.stepSummary: ינאי tells his wife to fear neither the פרושים nor those who are not פרושים. She should fear only the hypocrites who act like זמרי and want the reward of פנחס.
steps.simpleTranslation: King ינאי said to his wife: Do not be afraid of the פרושים, and not of those who are not פרושים. Be afraid only of the hypocrites who look like פרושים, because they act like זמרי and ask for a reward like פנחס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that backs up the theme: the real danger is the fake צדיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ינאי says the danger comes neither from the real פרושים nor from those who are not פרושים. The danger is the hypocrites who only look like פרושים, because they do wicked acts like זמרי but expect to be rewarded like פנחס.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked prince who sinned publicly in במדבר 25
The zealot who stopped זמרי and was rewarded

steps.whatToRemember: The list of פרושים is all about one danger: looking righteous on the outside without being righteous inside.

phrases.english: King Yannai said to his wife:
Do not be afraid of the Pharisees,
and not of those who are not Pharisees,
rather, of the hypocrites who look like Pharisees,
whose actions are like the deed of Zimri
and who ask for a reward like Pinchas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's warning with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The real danger is hypocrites who look like פרושים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: merit does not delay the bitter water
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי שמעון says זכות does not delay the punishment of the bitter water. If it did, women would stop fearing the water and innocent women would get a bad name.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון says: Merit does not delay the punishment of the bitter water. If you say merit does delay the cursing water, you weaken the water in the eyes of all the women who drink. And you give a bad name to the innocent women who drank, because people will say: 'They are guilty, only their merit held off the punishment.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי שמעון rejects the earlier view that a woman's merit can delay the water's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said a woman's זכות could delay the punishment. רבי שמעון gives two problems with that. First, guilty women will not fear the water, since they will rely on their merit. Second, innocent women who survive will be suspected, because people will say only merit saved them.

keyTerms.meaning: The bitter water that the סוטה drinks
Weakens, makes it lose its force

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not arguing about whether the woman is guilty. He is arguing about whether her good deeds can hold off the water's effect.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Shimon says:
Merit does not delay the bitter water.
And if you say
that merit delays the cursing water,
you weaken the water
in the eyes of all the women who drink.
And you give a bad name
to the innocent women who drank,
because people say: They are guilty,
only their merit delayed it for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זְכוּת תּוֹלָה בְּמַיִם הַמָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the aggadic discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, merit does not delay the effect of the bitter water.

steps.title: רבי: merit delays it, but she slowly wastes away
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that זכות does delay the punishment. But the woman cannot have children and does not thrive. She slowly gets worse and in the end dies the same death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Merit does delay the cursing water. But she does not give birth and does not flourish. Instead she slowly wastes away, and in the end she dies that same death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with רבי שמעון and explains what happens to a guilty woman whose merit delays the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי answers רבי שמעון's worry. A guilty woman protected by merit is clearly marked: she cannot have children and slowly declines. So no one will mix her up with an innocent woman, who stays healthy.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that merit does not delay the water. רבי holds that it does, but the guilty woman slowly declines and dies.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Merit delays the cursing water,
but she does not give birth and does not flourish,
rather she keeps wasting away,
and in the end she dies that same death.
phrases.notes: The same death a guilty סוטה dies right away from the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: הַזְּכוּת תּוֹלָה בְּמַיִם הַמְאָרְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי שמעון and answers his concerns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Merit delays the punishment, but the woman declines and eventually dies.

steps.title: A סוטה's מנחה that became טמא
steps.stepSummary: If her מנחה became טמא before it was made holy in a כלי שרת, it is redeemed. If it became טמא after, it is burned, just like all other מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her מנחה became טמא before it was made holy in the vessel, it is like all other מנחות and is redeemed. If it became טמא after it was made holy in the vessel, it is like all other מנחות and is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new law: what happens if the סוטה's מנחה becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key moment is when the flour is placed in the כלי שרת. Before that it is only promised to הקדש, so it can be redeemed and the money used. After that it has holiness of its own, so if it becomes טמא it cannot be redeemed and must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Her מנחה, the flour offering the סוטה brings
Became holy by being put into a כלי שרת

phrases.english: If her meal-offering became impure
before it was sanctified in the vessel,
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is redeemed.
And if after it was sanctified in the vessel,
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמֵאת מִנְחָתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָדְשָׁה בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה's מנחה follows the rule of all מנחות: redeemed if it became טמא before קדושת כלי, burned if after.

steps.title: Introducing the list of women whose מנחות are burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a list of women whose מנחות are burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the women whose מנחות are burned:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה is getting ready to list the women whose מנחות are burned, and the list comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after teaching that a מנחה is burned once it has become holy in the כלי, the משנה starts listing the cases where this happens. This line only opens the list; the cases themselves follow.

phrases.english: And these are the ones whose meal-offerings are burned:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a list that builds on the burning rule in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the cases of women whose מנחות are burned.
